newsitem.title: USA: "MarketSite" puts face on Nasdaq stock market.
newsitem.headline: "MarketSite" puts face on Nasdaq stock market.

text.p: Nasdaq on Monday launched MarketSite, a giant wall of computer screens aimed at putting a high-tech face on the stock market.

Although millions of shares are bought and sold every business day on Nasdaq, the shares trade unseen over computer systems. As a result, Nasdaq lacks the visual image of a trading floor packed with frantic businessmen and women jostling and waving tickets.

"We needed a place where there can be a focus on our markets, and this gives us the same kind of presence" as the New York Stock Exchange and the American Stock Exchange, Frank Zarb, president and chief executive of the National Association of Securities Dealers (NASD), told a news conference in New York Friday.

The $8 million wall of 100 monitors is located at Nasdaq's New York office, 33 Whitehall Street in Manhattan, a stone's throw from the New York Stock Exchange and American Stock Exchange buildings. It allows journalists to broadcast live "from the Nasdaq" with market data such as real-time stock prices, market volume and charts behind them.
"Investors will be more closely in touch with our marketplace and more people can understand (it)," Zarb said.

The news media can also link up for interviews with market-makers or brokerage trading floors, including Prudential Securities. There are also scrolling stock prices which use company logos, in order to be more investor-friendly, instead of their esoteric ticker symbols.
"This helps symbolize the marriage of New York as the financial capital of the world as well as the new media center of the world," New York Gov. George Pataki said Monday.
While he held the remote control, New York City Mayor Rudolph Giuliani pushed a button to turn on the 55-foot by 16-foot wall.
It was a favorable day for the launch. The Nasdaq rose more than 1 percent Monday, adding 14.62 to close at 1,251.35.
